requirements.statement: The journey's address-return route accepts a return only when its fulfilment id names a role and its handshake token matches the single-use token the picker issued for that role, a missing, reused or mismatched token included, and looks the returned address id up in the signed-in organisation's own address book.
requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party reads back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address, under a card titled 'Consignment addresses'. The plants frontend's check-answers place of destination, consignor and contact cards read back the same way, in the same increment: the name, then one line per address line, then the country, with no telephone number and no email address row.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting, and the owner's 17 November decision gives the addresses the same wording on check your answers, the overview task list and the addresses page. Plants has the same party cards, so it takes the same change at the same time (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), which withdraws plants' own d-013 addition of telephone and email to the contact card (c-293). The address-book record still carries both.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included (trace-e2e-p8-004, trace-e2e-p8-018), and the review already carries a 'Consignment addresses' card (repo-tests-p7-067). Plants' party cards today carry Name, Address, Telephone number and Email address rows with the address joined by commas, and lose telephone and email and read line by line in the same increment (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-045); the plants repo claims that show today's cards sit in the party-cards area's working set, not this one. The overview-and-review area writes the same card title, so the cross-area pass merges the two.

requirements.statement: Each party a notification holds has its own page for editing the copy the notification holds: in live animals one each for the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination at /notifications/<journeyId>/<party>/edit, reached from the party's 'Edit details' link on the Consignment addresses page and from the review page's error for a broken copy; in the high-risk plants frontend the same page serves the consignor, the place of destination and the consignment contact, reached from the picker's current-address card and from check your answers.
requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today in both frontends: five edit pages in live animals, which holds no consignment contact party (repo-frontend-p15-151, repo-frontend-p15-152), and three in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-052), reached from the 'Edit details' links (repo-tests-p7-055, repo-tests-p7-056, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-116, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-117). The older traces still show a live animals contact edit page (trace-e2e-p8-031). The design shows no such page; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.statement: The party edit page asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code' (width 10), 'Country' (a plain select, 'Select a country' then the address book's country list by name, saving the code), 'Phone number' (a telephone input with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code') and 'Email address' (an email input with spellcheck off), in that order; only address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The page sets every field the address book record carries, so a corrected copy loses nothing. Its Country stays a plain select in this programme: the animals party address country's autocomplete is a follow-on ticket recorded in deferred.md (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Built today with these nine fields in this order in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-100, repo-frontend-p15-101, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-056, repo-tests-p7-059, trace-e2e-p8-035 to trace-e2e-p8-044). requirements.statement: The party edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel', with no save-and-return-to-overview control and no task-list caption, progress or hub link of its own.
requirements.why: The page is an aside from a picker, the addresses page or the review, not a step of the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-120, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-072, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-130, trace-e2e-p8-045).

requirements.statement: The party edit page opens pre-filled with every field of the notification's copy, the country select set to its code; before any address is picked for that party, opening or posting it sends the trader to the party's picker and saves nothing, and in plants a party the notification's commodity does not owe, such as a potato notification's consignor, is sent to the picker too.
requirements.why: There is nothing to edit until a copy exists, and nothing to edit for a party the notification does not hold.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-121, repo-frontend-p15-131, repo-frontend-p15-106-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-080, repo-tests-p7-058, trace-e2e-p8-034).

requirements.statement: The party edit page applies the address book's rules and messages: 'Enter a name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' for a blank country, 'Enter a telephone number', 'Enter an email address', plus the length caps and the email-format check, with address line 2 and county never required and no rule on the shape of a phone number.
requirements.why: The copy must meet the same rules the address book sets, so a corrected copy is valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-110 to repo-frontend-p15-119, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-048, trace-e2e-p8-051), and plants copies the same rules and sentences from the address book (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-093, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-115). Both frontends label the postcode 'Postcode or Zip code' while its messages name only a postcode (repo-frontend-p15-115, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-104), which stays the address book's own wording.

requirements.statement: A refused edit answers 400, re-renders 'Edit address details' with the error summary and an error on each field, each summary link moving focus to its field, keeps what was typed (the country select resets to 'Select a country' for an unlisted value) and saves nothing; browser validation is off, every field is validated on every save, and a trader's own entry error is not logged as a refusal.
requirements.why: A refused edit must leave the notification's copy as it was, and the owner's 26 October decision is that a save with a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered kept.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-130, repo-frontend-p15-133, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-136, repo-tests-p7-064, trace-e2e-p8-047, trace-e2e-p8-053).

requirements.statement: A valid edit replaces only this notification's copy of the party: the address book record and any other notification holding a copy of it are unchanged, nothing is sent to the address book, the party's picker opens with no address preselected, and no banner is shown.
requirements.why: The copy belongs to the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-122 to repo-frontend-p15-124, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-082, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-083, repo-tests-p7-060, repo-tests-p7-061, repo-tests-p7-062, trace-e2e-p8-028).

requirements.statement: Save changes, Cancel and Back on the party edit page return to where the edit was started, named by its return marker from a closed list, carrying the trail: in live animals the Consignment addresses page or the review page, falling back to the Consignment addresses page; in plants check your answers or one of its three party pickers, falling back to the party's own picker, never an outside address. Cancel is acted on before anything is checked and discards what was typed.
requirements.why: The trader comes back to the page they left, and a return value from the request is never followed off the service.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-153, repo-frontend-p15-154, repo-frontend-p15-129, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-135, repo-tests-p7-065, trace-e2e-p8-057). The older traces still show a live animals return to the consignment contact picker (trace-e2e-p8-046-m1, trace-e2e-p8-058), which the journey no longer has (repo-frontend-p15-152).

requirements.statement: If saving an edit fails with a recoverable backend error, the party edit page re-renders with status 500 and the recoverable-error message, and the held copy is unchanged.
requirements.why: A failed save must not lose or corrupt the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-132, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-090, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-136).

requirements.statement: The party edit page has Welsh copy for every piece of wording it shows, the character-limit sentences included, marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.

requirements.deltaNote: Present in both frontends and marked as a machine draft (repo-frontend-p15-142, repo-frontend-p15-172, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-127, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-128).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is built only from GOV.UK Frontend components and has no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-140, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-124, trace-animals-fit-p15-067).

requirements.statement: A copy is checked against the notification's address rules: the address book accepts a record the rules refuse (such as a country name rather than a listed code), the picker lets the trader pick it, and its edit form then opens with no country selected.
requirements.why: The address book only checks a country is present, so the notification must catch a copy that breaks its rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-109, repo-frontend-p15-134-m1, trace-e2e-p8-013, trace-e2e-p8-022), and plants can check a held copy the same way (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-126).

requirements.statement: On the review page an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules is named in a 'There is a problem' error summary ('Correct the address details for the <role>'), linked to that party's edit page with return=notification-view and repeated inside the party's row; a stored answer that has become invalid is named on its card; these entries come before the unfinished-card entries, and either stops Continue. A party not yet chosen is not flagged.
requirements.why: The trader must see which copy to correct and get straight to it. The single-app prototype holds no copy that can break a rule, so it cannot express these errors (c-139).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today end to end (trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-016, trace-e2e-p8-017, trace-e2e-p8-019), and plants links its own check-answers refusal straight to the party's edit page (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-118).

requirements.statement: While a copy breaks the rules, Continue on the review page is refused (400, same error summary) and a direct declaration submit is refused and sent back to the review page.
requirements.why: A notification with an invalid party address must not be submitted, and the review page is where submission is refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-020, trace-e2e-p8-020-m1, trace-e2e-p8-021).

requirements.statement: Correcting the copy on its edit page and saving returns to the review page with the error gone, after which the trader can continue to the Declaration and submit to 'Import notification submitted'.
requirements.why: Correction must unblock submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-023, trace-e2e-p8-024).

requirements.statement: Once a notification is submitted its copied addresses are frozen: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record changes neither the submitted view, whose status tag reads 'Submitted' and which offers no Change or Edit details links, nor an amendment, neither shows an error, and cancelling the amendment restores the submitted copy.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is a record of what was declared, and a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other, no separate status being introduced.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-081, trace-e2e-p8-084, trace-e2e-p8-085), with one gap: no source edits a copy during an amendment and then cancels it (trace-e2e-p8-097).

requirements.statement: Until the address lookup is built, every add-address page reached from the journey opens on the address form with the address and contact fields and the 'Add to your address book' checkboxes shown at once, with no postcode step and no 'Enter address manually' link, so a trader can add any party's address by hand.
requirements.why: Ruling 2026-10-09 blocks address search on the address lookup becoming a real feature and ruling 2026-11-09 parks it as concept work, while manual address entry is built now; a destination-side page that sent the trader to a postcode step that does not exist would leave no way to add the address.
requirements.deltaNote: The page shows its nine fields and, from a party picker, the roles checkboxes at once for every role, with no lookup (repo-tests-p7-015, repo-tests-p7-027, repo-tests-p7-031), which is what the owner's 9 November decision keeps (ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-014).

requirements.statement: A trader adding an address from a germinal products notification's party picker crosses to the INS address book by the same handshake and the same add page, with the same address record and rules as live animals. The INS address book accepts the germinal products set as well as live animals, and saving or cancelling returns to the germinal set's own address-return page under /germinal-products/notifications/{notification id}, built on the server from a registered entry in the INS service's conventions, never to a live-animals notification.
requirements.why: Germinal products is a sibling set with its own journey, routes and cookies that takes live animals as its reference point for everything, and its notifications keep GBN-AG references; ruling 2026-10-09 puts the address-book return entry for the germinal set in the INS themes, proven in the ins Playwright project.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake carries journey-type 'gbn-ag' and the INS address book returns to the live-animals journey's address-return route (trace-e2e-p9-014, trace-e2e-p9-070, repo-frontend-p15-159); no germinal set exists yet.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: address search results that appear as the trader types, with the typed text in bold.
requirements.why: The design's address lookup is now the GOV.UK addresses pattern: the trader types a postcode, presses 'Find address' and chooses from a list on the next page, so nothing appears as they type. Design's 13 November decision had already settled that address search does not filter as the trader types.

requirements.statement: When the add page is reached from the journey, it skips the address book's 'Choose an address type' step and opens the address form for the type the party implies, with that party's role already held as one of the address's roles.
requirements.why: The section the trader came from already says what kind of address it is (DR1 inc-053, c-106's outcome); asking again would be a wasted step, and the address type is the front door's grouping of roles rather than anything stored, so the role the page was reached for settles it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no type step at all: the journey lands straight on the address and contact fields (trace-e2e-p9-055, repo-tests-p7-027). The skip is new logic that must ship with the address book's type step (address-book-add-and-edit).

requirements.statement: A picker search that matches nothing ('No addresses match your search.') still shows the 'Add a new address' control beside the picker's heading, so a trader whose address is not in the book can add it from there.
requirements.why: DR1 found the empty search a dead end (inc-053); the add control now sits beside the picker's heading whatever the search finds.
requirements.deltaNote: The picker renders the add control beside its heading whenever the service is not in stub mode, independent of the search results, and shows 'No addresses match your search.' in place of the count (repo-frontend-p15-056, repo-frontend-p15-036, repo-frontend-p15-023). The empty-state wording itself is the party picker area's.

requirements.statement: Each picker row offers a link to that saved address's own record in the INS address book, carrying the picker in a return parameter, with its search term, page, chosen address and trail, so the trader can correct or delete the book record and come back to the picker as they left it, under a column headed by the visually hidden word 'Actions'.
requirements.why: DR1 asked for a way to correct a wrong saved address from the picker (inc-054), built together with the add route and leading to the same place; the INS frontend is the address book's only writer (c-106), so the record and its edit live there.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: each row offers a 'View' link named for the address, going to the INS address book's own page for the record with a return query naming the picker, its search term, its page, the chosen address and the trail, under an 'Actions' column shown only outside stub mode (repo-frontend-p15-034, repo-frontend-p15-035, repo-frontend-p15-035-m1, repo-frontend-p15-026, repo-frontend-p15-036). The in-place 'View details' disclosure DR1 found, still in the older traces, has gone with it (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-036, trace-e2e-p8-093). Animals only: plants is not wired to the INS address book (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). What is left is the proof, because the fit suite runs in stub mode where the link is not offered (repo-frontend-p15-146).

requirements.statement: Out of scope here: transporter list rows linking to a saved transporter's own record page.
requirements.why: A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service rather than an Address, and it holds no role, so the link DR1 asked for on the transporter list belongs to the transporter work and not to this area's address pickers.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the plants frontend takes no part in the add-address round trip or the add page reached from the journey.
requirements.why: Plants is not wired to the INS address book and has no handshake today, and a row with no plants equivalent leaves plants alone (ruling 2026-10-09 pm); increments are not split to look for a plants equivalent. Plants does have the party edit page and the review read-back, so it takes those changes in the same increment (req-680 to req-693).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page reached from a party picker, 'Save and return to address page' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and select': with any answer missing or not valid the trader stays on the add-address page, sees an error for each one in field order, keeps every value they entered and every role they ticked, and nothing is written to the address book; the address is saved only once every answer passes. A germinal products notification's add-address page behaves the same way.
requirements.why: A second save button must not let a half-checked address into the trader's address book. The owner's 26 October decision is that the save buttons behave consistently, that a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, and that no page is an exception; the 10 November review restates that both save buttons make the same checks, and the owner's 27 November decision keeps that both save buttons on a page make the same checks in live animals, in the germinal products copy and on plants' pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Both save buttons are on the page today (repo-tests-p7-003) and a refused save keeps the page, lists the errors in field order and stores nothing; the tests drive that refusal from 'Save and return to address page' on the consignee route (repo-tests-p7-034, repo-tests-p7-035), while the design's suite lists the errors only from 'Save and select' (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-064) and its trace never shows the second save refused for the destination-side pages (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-073). What is left is proving the same refusal from 'Save and select' and from every role's page, and the germinal copy. The second save button itself is req-673 and the check set it applies is req-660 to req-668.

requirements.statement: The add-address page asks for 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and the postcode field, which the trader may leave blank.
requirements.why: The ruling of 14 October 2026 keeps County on the address book's add-details step, which is the step the journey's add-address page is: the V4 Address Block gives every address block the same fields, County included, and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose that data on a round trip.
requirements.deltaNote: The page already offers 'County (optional)' in that position, as a half-width input the trader may leave blank (repo-tests-p7-015, trace-e2e-p9-062, trace-e2e-p9-062-m1). Its length cap is req-668's 100 characters.

requirements.statement: On the consignee, importer and place of destination party edit pages the Country select holds 'United Kingdom' alone and the saved country is United Kingdom; the place of origin and consignor edit pages, and plants' consignor and contact edit pages, offer the whole country list. The plants frontend's place of destination edit page holds 'United Kingdom' alone too.
requirements.why: The address book refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom and leaves the other roles unrestricted, so a copy edit that could set another country would make the notification hold an address the book itself would not accept.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all five live animals edit pages apply the same nine rules with the same full country list and nothing depends on which party is being edited (repo-frontend-p15-155, repo-frontend-p15-103), and plants' edit page accepts any country the address book lists, the United States included (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-107, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-069).

requirements.statement: On the party edit page a country the address book does not list is refused with 'Enter a country' in both the live animals and the high-risk plants frontends.
requirements.why: The two frontends show the same page and both take their labels and refusals from the address book, so one unlisted country must not read two ways.
requirements.deltaNote: Live animals refuses both a blank and an unlisted country with 'Enter a country' (repo-frontend-p15-116, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-051), while plants refuses a blank one with 'Enter a country' and an unlisted one with 'Enter a valid country' (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-105, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-106).

requirements.statement: The party edit page's county field carries the browser autocomplete hint address-level1, as its other address fields carry theirs.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask an input holding personal data to identify its purpose, and the county is the only address field on the page without a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals edit form sets organization, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, tel and email but nothing on the county (repo-frontend-p15-105, trace-animals-fit-p15-053); plants already sets address-level1 (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-075), so only live animals changes.

requirements.statement: The add-address hand-off between the animals frontend and the INS address book works in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack the pull request end-to-end runs use, each service taking the other's address from its own configuration and never from a hard-coded host or port; the end-to-end suite proves it in the local and CI Docker stacks, and no new check of it is built for CDP.
requirements.why: Every link, redirect and form hand-over between services has to work in all three places from each service's own config (ruling 2026-11-04 point 4), and this hand-off is a redirect out of one service and back again. The owner's 27 November decision on the INS-to-journey hand-over sets how such a hand-over is proved (c-398).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hand-off is exercised where both frontends run, the compose stack and CDP, and skipped when the animals frontend runs in stub mode (repo-tests-p7-001, repo-frontend-p15-036, trace-e2e-p9-079); nothing names the CI Docker stack the pull request runs use as a place it is proven, and nothing shows either service reading the other's address from its own configuration.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page reached from a consignment contact page, with its own primary button label.
requirements.why: The live animals journey holds five parties and no consignment contact party, so no add-address page is reached from a contact page, and the design shows no contact address page either; every add-address page reached from the journey is reached from a party picker and reads 'Save and select' (req-671). The DR1 contact-page add link has no page to sit on (c-399).
requirements.deltaNote: The live animals party list holds no contact party, so there is no contact picker, contact edit page or contact route into the add page (repo-frontend-p15-152).

requirements.statement: The tests that prove the review page's broken-copy error summary and its inline party errors find the review's cards by GOV.UK structure and role rather than by the words of a numbered heading.
requirements.why: The owner's 19 November decision is that live animals review tests find cards the way the plants tests already do, so renumbering or rewording a card heading does not break a test of the address errors.
